quickAnswer: Ayer is a renter's town: 30.3% of households rent (ACS 2022), the 7th-highest share of the 50 towns we serve, and 35.7% of homes sit in multi-unit buildings. Only 16.9% heat with oil, so gas and electricity heat most homes.
body: ## Where three in ten households rent

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) finds 1,124 renter households among Ayer's 3,709 occupied homes. That is 30.3%, against 16.4% for the middle of the 50 MetroWest towns we serve, and it puts Ayer 7th. Owners number 2,585 (69.7%). Ayer is also 6th for multi-unit housing: 1,379 of 3,863 units (35.7%) are in multi-unit buildings, including 772 units (20.0%) in buildings of five or more, 321 (8.3%) in buildings of three or four and 286 (7.4%) in two-unit buildings.

Only 1,970 units (51.0%) are single-family detached houses, 47th of 50. Townhouse-style homes add 483 (12.5%) and mobile homes 31 (0.8%). The median value of an owner-occupied home is $393,000, also 47th, and the middle town sits at $579,150. Vacancy is 4.0% (154 units).
## Gas and electricity do most of the heating

Ayer differs from the middle town. Utility gas heats 2,186 homes (58.9%), 10th-highest of the 50 towns, and electricity heats 754 (20.3%), 7th-highest, with 10.1% for the middle town. Fuel oil heats only 628 (16.9%), 45th of 50. Bottled gas heats 86 homes (2.3%).

For a decision in a rental building, that spread matters. In a gas building, a like-for-like gas boiler is often the simplest replacement. In an electric-heat building, a heat pump can be worth pricing. With oil at 16.9%, the oil-or-switch question comes up less in Ayer than in towns where oil is the leading fuel.
## An 1871 railroad junction

The Wikipedia history says Ayer was incorporated on February 14, 1871, partitioned from Groton, and had been known as Groton Junction and later Ayer Junction. In only 9.5 square miles it became a major junction for east-west and north-south rail lines, with the Fitchburg Railroad arriving in 1844. Camp Devens was established in 1917, later Fort Devens, and commercial development followed the base until it closed in 1996. The town was named for Dr. James Cook Ayer, who funded the construction of Town Hall. During the Civil War an army training camp, Camp Stevens, stood near the Nashua River, and the Nashua River Rail Trail has occupied the old Worcester and Nashua right-of-way since 2005.

At the newer end, 425 units (11.0%) went up in 2010 or later, 12th highest of the 50 towns, and the median year built is 1975. The Wikipedia text also mentions Vitasoy and Pepsi plants, a historic downtown and modern commuter rail service to Boston.
## Landlords, tenants and a pre-war core

A boiler that fails in a building with several households leaves all of them cold, so the person making the call is often the owner of a rental building rather than an occupant. In Ayer, 826 units (21.4%) date from 1939 or earlier, 13th highest of the 50 towns, and 2,209 (57.2%) predate 1980. In buildings of those eras the pipework and flues may be original or replaced in stages, which is one reason to look at each building before choosing a replacement.
## National Grid and the rebates

Ayer is in National Grid's Massachusetts Electric Company territory, so Mass Save is the rebate route for many customers here. With a fifth of homes already on electric heat, the [heat pump page](/cities/ayer/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) is worth a read for owners and landlords alike.

faq.a: Compared with most towns we serve, yes. Oil or kerosene heats 628 occupied homes (16.9%), 45th of 50, against 36.5% in the middle town. Bottled gas heats 86 (2.3%). Utility gas and electricity are the main fuels, so most replacement quotes here compare gas with a heat pump.

faq.q: Is gas the usual heating fuel in Ayer?
faq.a: Yes. Utility gas heats 58.9% of occupied homes, well above the 41.9% of the middle town. A main on your street is still not guaranteed, so ask the gas company about your address, or raise it when we give the estimate.

faq.q: Do Ayer homes qualify for Mass Save heat pump rebates?
faq.a: They can. National Grid serves the town and sponsors Mass Save, and the home has to be weatherized enough first. The rules and amounts change from year to year, so read the heat pump page and confirm at masssave.com before you commit to a contract.

faq.q: Ayer homes are worth less than the middle town. Does that matter for a new system?
faq.a: The median owner-occupied home is $393,000, 47th of 50 and well under the middle town's $579,150. A heating system is a large purchase on any house, so comparing a like-for-like replacement and a heat pump side by side in writing is worth the time. Our estimates are free and written.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Utility gas heats 2,186 Ayer homes and electricity 754, with oil far behind, and 1,379 units sit in multi-unit buildings. A failed boiler can leave several households cold, and a gas job needs a permit.
body: ## Replacing heat in a gas-first town

Utility gas heats 58.9% of Ayer homes, 10th highest of the 50 towns and well above the 41.9% of the middle town. Where a building is on gas and the venting and piping are sound, a gas-for-gas replacement is often the straightforward route. Bottled gas serves only 86 homes (2.3%), 42nd of 50, so tank deliveries are not a big part of the picture.
### The permit step

Anyone who pulls a gas permit in Massachusetts must be a licensed plumber or gas fitter. A new gas furnace or boiler is normally inspected before it is signed off. The building department can describe the local procedure, and your installer should say who is filing the paperwork before the job begins.
### One boiler, several households

Buildings of three or four units hold 321 Ayer homes and buildings of five or more hold 772. In a building like that, one boiler may serve many households. The replacement may have to be scheduled around when tenants can be without heat, and the piping may need a pressure test before the system returns to service.
### Questions that shape the job
- What fuel is the system on, and how old is it?
- Does the building have one system or several?
- Is it owner-occupied, rented or part of an association?
- Radiators, baseboard or ducts?
### Houses from 1960 to 1979

The 907 units from 1960 to 1979 (23.5%) sit between the pre-war core and the newer stock. Their load depends on insulation, windows and the number of floors, and we measure that load before pricing a new boiler or furnace instead of repeating the old unit's size.
### Emergency line
If the heat fails, call (508) 786-8755. We take emergency calls 24 hours a day.

faq.q: Is it better to repair or replace a gas boiler in an older building?
faq.a: It depends on age and the fault. A young boiler with one failed part is worth repairing. A cracked heat exchanger, or repeated repairs on an old unit, usually point to replacement. With 826 Ayer units from 1939 or earlier, many boilers are in older buildings, so ask for both options in writing.

faq.q: How do I plan a boiler replacement in a building with tenants?
faq.a: Give tenants the dates in advance, and if possible schedule the work for a stretch of mild weather. About 30.3% of Ayer households rent, so this comes up often. Ask the installer how long the heat will be off and whether temporary heaters are needed.

faq.q: Can I move from electric baseboard to gas?
faq.a: Only if a gas main reaches the building and the venting can be arranged, and with 20.3% of Ayer homes on electric heat, many owners ask. A heat pump is the other option, since it needs no gas line. We assess the heating load of the home before quoting either one.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Only 51.0% of Ayer's housing units are detached houses, and 1,379 sit in multi-unit buildings. Ducts suit some of these buildings, and a separate ductless unit for each apartment suits many of the rest.
body: ## Cooling apartments, townhouses and houses

Ayer ranks 47th of the 50 towns for single-family detached housing, where the middle town has 76.7%. Detached houses number 1,970, townhouse-style homes 483, two-unit buildings 286 and buildings of three or four units 321. The largest group after detached houses is 772 units in buildings of five or more, and the answer to a cooling question changes with the building.
### Apartments

A separate ductless system in each apartment lets every household run its own cooling, which matters most where tenants pay their own electric bill. A failed unit does not leave the whole building without cooling. Window units are one alternative, but they block light and need removing for winter.
Of the 3,863 units, 1,970 are detached. The rest span attached homes, small multi-unit buildings and larger blocks, so a cooling job in Ayer is about as likely to be an apartment as a house.
### Attached homes
Townhouse-style homes share walls and may have less outdoor space. An outdoor condenser has to fit the lot and any association rules. A ductless unit with a short line set is often the simplest fit.
A mini-split can add cooling to a finished townhouse-style home without opening walls, which suits the median 1975 building.
### Detached houses and mobile homes

A detached house can usually take central air if the ducts are in good condition. In houses heated by radiators, there are no ducts to reuse, and a ductless mini-split avoids ductwork entirely. The 31 mobile homes (0.8%) are limited by layout and space, so equipment choices there are narrower.
### What shapes a cooling plan
- The rooms that run hot.
- Where the outdoor unit can sit.
- Electrical capacity at the panel.
- Whether a heat pump could serve both seasons.
### Electric homes

A fifth of Ayer's homes already heat with electricity, so one heat pump can cover heating and cooling for them. The [heat pump page](/cities/ayer/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) has the program route.

faq.q: Can a landlord install ductless cooling in each Ayer apartment?
faq.a: Often yes. Each apartment gets its own outdoor and indoor unit, so tenants control their own cooling. The building layout, wall access and electrical capacity decide the details, and in larger buildings the owner has to agree where outdoor units go.

faq.q: Is central air practical for an older Ayer house with radiators?
faq.a: It needs new ducts, which can be a bigger job in a finished house. With 21.4% of the town's units built in 1939 or earlier, many owners ask this. A ductless mini-split avoids ductwork entirely, so it is often the first option priced.

faq.q: How do I size cooling for an apartment?
faq.a: From the unit itself, not from the label on an old air conditioner. Floor area, windows, which way the rooms face and the floor level all play a part. An oversized unit shuts off before it removes moisture, which leaves the apartment clammy instead of comfortable.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: National Grid serves Ayer and sponsors Mass Save, so its rebates are the usual route. With electricity heating 754 homes (20.3%, 7th of 50) and 1,379 units in multi-unit buildings, the town has many heat pump candidates.
body: ## National Grid territory, many electric homes

Ayer appears in National Grid's Massachusetts Electric Company territory. For 2026 the whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500, once the home has been weatherized. The rest of the rules are on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Where the gain is largest

Electric heat is the clearest target. Electricity heats 754 Ayer homes, 7th highest of the 50 towns and double the 10.1% of the middle town. A heat pump moves heat instead of making it, so for baseboard or electric furnace households it is a different way to use the same utility. Oil serves 628 homes and bottled gas 86, and the 55 homes on other fuel or coal may also want a look.
### Gas homes

Gas is the largest group at 2,186 homes. For them the comparison is between a new gas system and a heat pump, and a household with a failing boiler and no cooling can price one heat pump project against two purchases.
### Age against the 2000 line

The weatherization test accepts houses built in 2000 or later, and Ayer has 717 such units (18.6%), including 425 (11.0%) from 2010 on. The 57.2% built before 1980 need an assessment or completed work, and a Home Energy Assessment is the practical first step there.
### Rental buildings

For landlords, a ductless mini-split can heat and cool a single apartment. Confirm who pays the electric bill, since tenant-paid and landlord-paid systems differ. A whole-home rebate is one per customer account, so owners of multi-unit property should ask how it applies.
### Ducted or ductless
Ducted units reuse good ductwork, and ductless heads suit apartments, additions and rooms with none. With 1,970 detached houses and 1,379 multi-unit homes, both layouts are common.

faq.q: Can I get the Mass Save rebate on a rental property in Ayer?
faq.a: It depends on how the account is set up and who the customer is. The rebate is limited to one whole-home rebate per customer account, so ask Mass Save how it applies to a multi-unit building before you commit. Ayer has 1,124 renter households, so this question is common.

faq.q: Is a heat pump a good fit for electric baseboard homes?
faq.a: Often. A heat pump moves heat rather than creating it, so it can deliver the same warmth with less electricity than resistance heat. The result depends on the house, so we do not quote a saving. With 20.3% of Ayer homes on electric heat, many owners start here.

faq.q: Does the home need weatherization first?
faq.a: For the whole-home rebate, yes, unless it was built in 2000 or later. A Home Energy Assessment that recommends under $1,000 of work meets the test, as does completing recommendations made in 2013 or later. Confirm the current terms at masssave.com before you plan the job.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Most Ayer systems run on gas or electricity, so a tune-up is a safety and efficiency check more than a soot cleaning. With 1,124 renter households, a fall visit is easier to plan than a night call.
body: ## Tune-ups for a gas and electric town

Gas and electricity head Ayer's fuel list, and oil is far down it. On a gas boiler or furnace the technician works through the burner, flue, controls and shutoffs. For electric systems and heat pumps, it covers filters, coils, drains and refrigerant-side readings. The 628 oil homes (16.9%) still need a yearly cleaning.
### Renters, owners and shared systems

Renters hold 1,124 of Ayer's 3,709 occupied homes (30.3%) and owners 2,585 (69.7%). The sanitary code asks rentals to hold 68 F between 7 a.m. and 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight during the heating season, and unless a lease says differently, the landlord supplies the heat. A boiler failure in a building with several households hits all of them, so a fall visit helps. This is general information, not legal advice.
### Old equipment in old buildings

Ayer has the 13th-highest share of homes built in 1939 or earlier, 826 units. Equipment in buildings of that age may be on a later replacement cycle, and a tune-up is a good moment to ask how many seasons remain. Another 476 units (12.3%) date from 1940 to 1959, and 937 (24.3%) from 1980 to 1999.
### Vacant units
The Census counts 154 vacant units (4.0%). Vacant units still have heating equipment, and a pre-season visit is a good way to confirm it will run when someone moves in.
### Calendar
- Late summer or early fall: heating.
- Spring: cooling and mini-splits.
- Any time: noise, smell, short cycling or an unusual bill.
### Before you call
Check the filter and the thermostat batteries, clear snow from outdoor units, and note the fuel, the system's age and what you noticed, so the visit can start with your actual symptoms.
If the visit shows the unit is near the end, the [heating page](/cities/ayer/heating-installation-repair) explains how we approach replacement.

faq.q: Does a gas boiler need a yearly tune-up?
faq.a: A yearly check before the heating season is a good habit. Utility gas heats 58.9% of Ayer homes, so this is the most common visit here. The burner, venting and safety controls should be inspected, and a technician can catch small faults before they turn into cold-weather failures.

faq.q: Who arranges maintenance in a multi-unit building?
faq.a: Usually the building owner or association, when the system serves several units. A system that serves only your unit may be your responsibility, so check your lease or condo documents. With 35.7% of Ayer units in multi-unit buildings, the answer varies from one building to the next.

faq.q: Do electric baseboard homes need a tune-up?
faq.a: Less than combustion systems. Baseboard has no burner, so the visit is mostly about cleaning dust from the elements, checking thermostats and looking at the wiring. A heat pump is different: it needs clean coils, filters and a clear condensate drain, and a technician can read the refrigerant side.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Ayer has 826 units built in 1939 or earlier, 425 built since 2010 and more than a third of homes sharing a building with neighbors. Leaky old buildings, tight new ones and shared walls each bring different air issues.
body: ## Air in a town of shared buildings

Ayer's housing runs from pre-1940 buildings to ones built since 2010, and 35.7% of units are in buildings with more than one unit. The town covers only 9.5 square miles, and in a shared building air can move from one unit to the next.
### Between apartments

Gaps, shared walls, halls and sometimes shared ducts can carry cooking odors, smoke and moisture between units. Sealing gaps, running bathroom and kitchen fans and changing filters help. Shared ductwork is the building owner's to examine, since one tenant cannot change it.
### Older buildings

The 826 pre-1940 units leak air through gaps, which lets some pollutants out and pulls dust, pollen and damp basement air in. Old ductwork can hold years of dust. Anyone renovating a pre-war unit should have a qualified specialist test for older materials first.
### Newer buildings

The 425 units from 2010 or later are tighter. That keeps energy in, and it also keeps moisture and chemicals from furnishings inside unless ventilation keeps up. A working bathroom fan and a range hood that vents outside help.
### Basements and winter dryness

Basements in older buildings may need a dehumidifier, while a leak or grading problem must be fixed at its source. In winter a humidifier tied to the system can help, as long as the setting stays moderate.

With 286 units in two-unit buildings (7.4%) and 321 in buildings of three or four, the person who controls the filter and the person who breathes the air are often not the same, so settle who changes filters and who calls about humidity.
### Filters and fuel alarms

Better filters help in every kind of building, but a higher-rated filter restricts airflow more, so the system has to be able to handle it. Other fuel or coal heats 55 Ayer homes, and any home that burns a fuel can benefit from a working carbon monoxide alarm.
### What we can do
- Upgrade filtration.
- Control humidity.
- Add or fix ventilation.
- Clean ducts that are visibly dirty or damaged.

faq.q: Can smoke or cooking odors come from a neighbor's apartment?
faq.a: Yes, through gaps, shared walls or shared ducts. With 1,379 Ayer units in multi-unit buildings, this happens often enough to be a regular question. Sealing gaps and running fans helps, and a building owner may need to address shared ductwork.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Rarely as a routine. Look inside first: mold, thick dirt or damage left by pests or building work are reasons to clean. Dust around a register more often points to a tired filter, so swap that before paying for anything larger. A technician can scope the ducts for you.

faq.q: Do small apartments need a ventilation fix?
faq.a: Often a small one. Apartments hold less air, so moisture and odors build up faster. A bathroom fan that runs, a kitchen hood that vents outside and a dehumidifier in damp months usually cover it. In a unit with a shared duct, the owner may need to help.
